## Computing the T-Statistic

In this section, we will demonstrate how to perform a *small sample inference for the mean* using the **Student’s t-distribution**.  
When the population standard deviation is unknown and the sample size is small (typically \( n < 30 \)), we use the *t-distribution* instead of the *normal distribution* to construct confidence intervals and perform hypothesis testing.  

We will consider an example where we have a small sample of data representing the lifetimes (in hours) of light bulbs produced by a factory.  
The goal is to determine whether the mean lifetime differs from the manufacturer’s claimed mean of 1000 hours.  
We will compute:
- The **sample mean** and **sample standard deviation**.  
- The **t-statistic** and **degrees of freedom**.  
- The **p-value** and the **confidence interval** for the mean.  
Finally, we visualize the **t-distribution** with the calculated statistic.

---

```{r, echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Set up the sample data
light_bulb_hours <- c(980, 995, 1005, 1020, 990, 1010, 1002, 1008, 995, 1003)

# Known hypothesized mean (manufacturer's claim)
mu0 <- 1000

# Sample size, mean, and standard deviation
n <- length(light_bulb_hours)
xbar <- mean(light_bulb_hours)
s <- sd(light_bulb_hours)

# Compute t-statistic
t_stat <- (xbar - mu0) / (s / sqrt(n))
df <- n - 1

# Compute p-value for a two-tailed test
p_value <- 2 * (1 - pt(abs(t_stat), df))

# Compute 95% confidence interval for the mean
alpha <- 0.05
t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha/2, df)
margin_error <- t_crit * (s / sqrt(n))
ci_lower <- xbar - margin_error
ci_upper <- xbar + margin_error

# Display results
cat("Sample Mean:", round(xbar, 2), "\n")
cat("Sample SD:", round(s, 2), "\n")
cat("t-Statistic:", round(t_stat, 3), "\n")
cat("Degrees of Freedom:", df, "\n")
cat("p-value:", round(p_value, 4), "\n")
cat("95% Confidence Interval: [", round(ci_lower, 2), ",", round(ci_upper, 2), "]\n")

# Visualization of t-distribution and test statistic
curve(dt(x, df), from = -4, to = 4, col = "blue", lwd = 2,
      main = "t-Distribution with Test Statistic",
      ylab = "Density", xlab = "t-value")

# Add vertical lines for critical and observed t-values
abline(v = c(-t_crit, t_crit), col = "red", lty = 2)
abline(v = t_stat, col = "darkgreen", lwd = 2)
legend("topright", legend = c("t PDF", "Critical t", "Observed t"),
       col = c("blue", "red", "darkgreen"), lwd = c(2, 1, 2), lty = c(1, 2, 1))
```
